verdict: Broadcom grew revenue 20% to a record $15.0B as AI chip sales jumped 46%, and net income more than doubled to $5.0B as the heavy costs of absorbing VMware faded.

kpis.label: AI semiconductor revenue
kpis.note: to over $4.4B — guided to $5.1B next quarter

segments.name: Semiconductor solutions
segments.note: Chips — above all custom AI accelerators and networking gear for data centers. AI semiconductor revenue grew 46% YoY to over $4.4B.

segments.name: Infrastructure software
segments.note: VMware and other enterprise software — the steady, subscription side of the company, up 25% YoY.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Designing the next chips and software — a smaller share of each revenue dollar than most chip rivals spend.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Selling the products and running the company.

opex.name: Amortization & restructuring
opex.note: Writing down the value of brands and technology bought in acquisitions (VMware above all) — a bookkeeping charge, not cash — plus restructuring costs.

otherDetail: Interest expense of $769M on Broadcom's debt, partly offset by $25M of other income — a net -$744M below operating profit.

takeaways.title: AI chips keep climbing
takeaways.text: AI semiconductor revenue grew 46% YoY to over $4.4B, and Broadcom guided it to $5.1B in the next quarter — a tenth straight quarter of AI growth, on custom accelerators and AI networking gear.

takeaways.title: VMware is the steady half
takeaways.text: Infrastructure software revenue rose 25% to $6.6B — 44% of all revenue — giving Broadcom a subscription base that smooths the ups and downs of chip sales.

takeaways.title: A cash machine
takeaways.text: Free cash flow was $6.4B — 43% of revenue — even while carrying the debt taken on to buy VMware; interest on that debt cost $769M in the quarter.

oneTimers: GAAP profit carries $1,989M of amortization of acquisition-related intangible assets ($1,483M inside cost of revenue and $506M inside operating expenses) — mostly bookkeeping from the VMware deal, not cash. On Broadcom's non-GAAP view, net income was $7,787M instead of $4,965M.
